result: PASS: no new material/marker/attachment defect observed in inspected captures
method: All96 original views inspected through four uniform crop/nearest-resize contact sheets; full original case43front additionally opened. Original bytes and hashes bound by original-provenance.json. This is a static visual pass, not a movie/multiplayer/shader/audio pass.

notes.observation: Young Hero with either Run setting and centered-Run older Hero have coherent blue orb pigmentation. Dark lower/side faces follow ordinary block lighting; no mixed atlas patches were observed.
At half maturity and maximum Run the Hero orb is purple-gray; at mature baby maximum Run it is pink. Those intentional intermediate/end hues match the independently inspected viewer progression.

Partial alignment shows gray-green marker tint while the fully Hero-weighted states show pink. Mod Hero influence reaches its endpoint at alignment +0.5, so raw +0.5 and +0.75 are expected to resemble full Hero in this prototype.

Ruby, Red shiny and Green mono retain the same developed pink Hero marker pigment despite different body colors. Red shiny shows a pronounced white/silver reflection across orb and body; the existing finish pass is preserved. This reflection is distinct from a texture/UV color patch.

Ruby body, rabbit replacements, phoenix wings and glasses remain coherent. Eyelens/frame placement follows the original face in the inspected views; the yellow Neutral orb does not become ruby red. Head additions are hidden by the existing acquired-head-part rule.

The skeleton skull covers the head/added features as intended; rabbit hand/foot replacements remain coherent and the Neutral orb stays yellow. The closed skull prevents inspection of the covered native eyes/head surfaces.

Existing Hero Run first-evolution short stem and mature three-branch crest/halo remain distinct with compact hands/feet and original box head/eyes. No unexpected exposed internal features were observed.

limitations: Reported original patchwork/strange-color artifact not independently reproduced. Intended gray/pink development and existing shiny silver reflection are retained.
Low-angle views partly occlude the orb behind the head; front/side/above angles show its exposed faces.
Static cameras show sampled states, not the complete motion/transition trajectory.
Covered head geometry under the skeleton skull cannot be visually assessed.
